2.why: Pitch 2 ends on a comfortable ledge at a double-bolt anchor after the traverse; MP agrees bolts
2.text: On a roomy ledge at the end of the rightward traverse, at a pair of bolts.

3.why: Pitch 3 ends at the top of the chimney on a ledge with a gear anchor; both sources agree
3.text: On the ledge at the top of the short chimney, built from gear.

4.why: Pitch 4 goes up the curving crack to the final anchor beneath the giant roof
4.text: At the final bolted station, tucked beneath the huge roof at the top of the arching crack.

P2.why: Source has no pitch numbers; the 5.10 corner and leftward traverse may be a different pitch than stored P2

P3.why: Source unnumbered; ledge after the roofs is a reconstruction, not placed at a numbered pitch end

1.why: Pitch 1: slab, then corner to a belay below a steep white face
1.text: Beneath a steep white face, at the top of the corner above the low-angle slab.

2.why: Pitch 2: face cracks trending left to a ledge below a sharp corner
2.text: On a ledge sitting under a sharp corner, after the long leftward-trending face cracks.

P1.why: P1 gully to belay in saddle overlooking east face, chain anchors
P1.text: In the saddle at the top of the gully, where it looks over the east face, on chain anchors.

P2.why: P2 groove, traverse onto Regular Route, 11 bolts to chains under a large bench
P2.text: At chains below a large bench, once the groove traverse joins the Regular Route.

P3.why: P3 knobby ramp to chain anchors in a basalt band
P3.text: At chain anchors set in the basalt band above the knobby ramp.
